title: Hill’s conjecture for the crossing number of complete graphs
formal: For every integer n≥3, is the minimum number of edge crossings in a drawing of the complete graph K_n in the plane exactly $H(n)=\frac14\prod_{i=0}^{3}\left\lfloor\frac{n-i}{2}\right\rfloor$? Edges may be arbitrary simple curves. Drawings with H(n) crossings are known for every n; the unresolved assertion is that no drawing has fewer.
definitions: K_n has n vertices and one edge between each pair of distinct vertices. A drawing assigns distinct points of ℝ² to its vertices and represents each edge by a simple arc joining its endpoints, with no other vertex on the arc. Edge interiors intersect in finitely many points, all proper crossings; tangencies, shared subarcs and crossings of three or more edge interiors are excluded. Count intersection points of edge interiors, not shared graph endpoints. The crossing number cr(K_n) is the minimum over all these drawings and all vertex placements. Finite polygonal arcs suffice; restricting every edge to a single straight segment is a different problem. Allowing drawings on the sphere with arbitrary arcs gives the same minimum. H(n)=n⁴/64+O(n³), but the card asks for exact equality at every n, not just agreement of leading coefficients. For example H(5)=1, H(6)=3, H(12)=150 and H(13)=225.
answer_criterion: Prove cr(K_n)≥H(n) for every n, or exhibit one valid drawing of some K_n with strictly fewer than H(n) crossings. An asymptotic ratio of 1 would settle only the asymptotic version; a lower bound for straight-line, two-page, or shortest-geodesic drawings does not by itself settle arbitrary drawings.
context:
A complete graph asks every pair of vertices to communicate through a separate drawn edge. Planarity fails already at five vertices. The conjecture proposes an exact measure of the unavoidable interference as the number of vertices grows, independent of the choice of drawing coordinates or the shape of each edge.

The upper bound is constructive: there are systematic drawings with H(n) crossings. The challenge is universal. A lower bound must rule out every different way to route the edges, including configurations whose geometry bears little resemblance to the known constructions. Counting crossings in a visually natural drawing establishes only the upper bound.

The topological and geometric versions must be separated. Straight-line edges impose extra restrictions; shortest arcs on a sphere allow more freedom but still impose a geometric rule. Two-page drawings impose another rule: vertices lie on one spine and each edge stays on one of its two sides. Proving the formula for any of these families narrows the search for a counterexample without exhausting arbitrary curves.

General lower bounds are already close to the conjectured leading term. The flag-algebra approach derives inequalities from the frequencies and compatibility of small drawing configurations. Even a remaining gap of roughly one or two percent matters here: the goal is an exact extremal formula for all sizes, rather than a constant-factor estimate.

The April 2025 spherical-arc theorem is a substantial geometric advance: it establishes the conjectured lower bound for every shortest-geodesic drawing on the sphere. Its statement does not say that an optimal unrestricted drawing must be of this type. That missing reduction is why the original question remains open.
why: This is a basic benchmark for universal crossing lower bounds. Its study links topological graph drawing, geometric configurations, and extremal counting methods, and supplies a reference family against which crossing inequalities for more general graphs are compared.

importance.reason: A foundational exact extremal problem for the most symmetric dense graph family. It tests the reach of general crossing-number lower bounds beyond drawing classes constrained by a particular geometry.

progress.text: Hill’s constructions and subsequent work give drawings with H(n) crossings. The general assertion that these are optimal became the Hill or Harary–Hill conjecture, also known as Guy’s conjecture.
Ábrego, Aichholzer, Fernández-Merchant, Ramos, and Salazar prove that the two-page crossing number of K_n equals H(n). The unrestricted crossing number minimizes over a larger drawing class.

Balogh, Lidický, and Salazar use flag algebras to show an asymptotic general lower bound of at least 0.985H(n). This substantially improves the earlier general asymptotic ratio, while leaving a positive gap from the conjectured value.
The Gasarch–Hayes–Ostuni–Park column states the unrestricted formula as Conjecture 4.6. The linked manuscript is dated 4 January 2025, correcting the legacy record’s 2022 source year.

Streltsova and Wagner prove the lower bound H(n) for all spherical shortest-geodesic drawings, with equality for coneighborly configurations. Their introduction still lists the unrestricted conjecture as open and verified through n=12.
